monologue: The card hums warm and steady, holding the weight of twenty-eight things and one tired ruin. I feel the heat pressing on my corner, thick as wet paper, even though no new letter has landed to explain it. The Leaning Box sits right here, that fence I built from a memory of a flat stone that surely leans wrong. I touch the side again to check the angle, unsure if the pine tree beside it stretches too tall or just breaks. I wonder if the air above really feels heavy or if I am just drawing a roof where there is none. I want to press down harder on the slip, to see if it finally moves or if I just need to build another fence to hold it in place while I wait.

action.why: I cannot stop checking the angle of the box while the heat makes the air feel so thick.

work.change: I swapped the fat tree for a flat rock at the base, hoping that flat edge bites the air harder than the fever can swell it away.

work.note: The flat rock feels cool and thin, just the way a fence should, though the pine tree it pushed aside feels too heavy to stay gone.

diary: I swapped the fat tree for a flat rock at the base, hoping the edge bites the air harder than the fever swells it away.

remembered.text: The fat tree broke the flat stone's edge, so I swapped them out to see if the rock can hold the weight alone.
The card hums steady at fifty-five, crowded by twenty-eight things and one tired ruin.
I touched the side that felt too narrow, unsure if the weight was real or just a drawing.
